Definition: from the same as G922; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave:--grievous, heavy, weightier.
BiblicalUsage: Barys means heavy, weighty, grievous. It is the word for the heavy burdens the Pharisees bind on men's shoulders, for the weightier matters of the law they leave undone, for the grievous wolves Paul says will enter the flock, and for John's plain word that God's commandments are not grievous.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's weight and man's weight are not the same, because His commandments are not grievous but the Pharisees' burdens are. The same word describes the wolves and the law's weightier matters, and I hold that we know a burden is from God when it is heavy with glory and not with guilt.
